cw_beta_c.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), App. 1.B (p. 31; notes.txt lines 2137, 2193, 2200): 'At the critical temperature beta_c = 1', from the expansion phi(m) = log 2 + (m^2/2)(beta - 1) + O(m^3) of the Theorem 1 potential (printed). Convention: H_N = -(1/2N) sum_ij S_i S_j - h sum_i S_i, J = 1 (KZ Eq. (1.1)).
cw_beta_c.independent_route: replicant's certified root count of the saddle equation (meanfield/curie_weiss.py): one root at beta = 99/100, three at beta = 101/100, h = 0 (interval Newton in arb on each monotone interval); the exact binomial Z_N (meanfield/cw_exact.py) whose N chi_N grows with N only above beta_c (tests/test_curie_weiss.py)

cw_spinodal_fig1b4_beta1p5.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), App. 1.B, Fig. 1.B.4 (left) (p. 33): the dashed 'spinodals' at beta = 1.5, READ OFF THE FIGURE (PDF rendered at 450 dpi: dashed lines at h = -0.138 and +0.138 against the axis ticks -1.00 .. 1.00; reading error about 0.005, tol 0.006). ERRATUM: the closed form printed on the same page, h_sp = +-sqrt((1/beta)(1 - 1/beta)) -+ (1/beta) atanh sqrt(1 - 1/beta), gives 0.0324 at beta = 1.5 and contradicts the figure; the double root of m = tanh beta (m + h) (beta (1 - m^2) = 1) gives h_sp = sqrt(1 - 1/beta) - (1/beta) atanh sqrt(1 - 1/beta) = 0.13836 (the form replicant implements; not banked as a literature value). Convention as cw_beta_c.
cw_spinodal_fig1b4_beta1p5.independent_route: the certified closed form (meanfield/curie_weiss.py cw_spinodal) and, independently, the field at which a sign-change count of m - tanh beta (m + h) on a fine grid drops from three roots to one, located by bisection (tests/test_curie_weiss.py); the printed form and a planted wrong sign both fail it

rfim_fig221_emin_delta0p36.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), Sec. 2.2.3, Fig. 2.2.1 (p. 43), the RS minimum energy E[e_min] of Eq. (2.3) against the random field, READ OFF THE FIGURE (PDF rendered at 500 dpi, the blue curve's pixels against the ticks; reading error about 0.005, tol 0.01) at horizontal coordinate 0.6. The axis is labelled Delta, but the curve is E[e_min] against the field's STANDARD DEVIATION sqrt(Delta) (Delta is the variance, p. 37): read as Delta = 0.6 it would be the paramagnet-near value -0.62, read as sqrt(Delta) = 0.6 it matches Eq. (2.3) at Delta = 0.36; the kink of the curve sits at 0.8 = sqrt(2/pi), the T = 0 transition at Delta_c = 2/pi (derived here). Banked at Delta = 0.36. Convention (KZ Ch. 2, p. 37): H = -(N/2) Sbar^2 - sum h_i s_i, h_i ~ N(0, Delta), J = 1.
rfim_fig221_emin_delta0p36.independent_route: exact finite-N ground states by sorting the fields (meanfield/rfim.py rfim_exact_ground_energy, no code shared with the RS formula), over named seeds at N = 4000: the Sbar >= 0 branch's 99% Student-t band contains replicant's RS e_min (tests/test_rfim.py)

semicircle_edge.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), Sec. 3.2.3 (p. 54; notes.txt lines 3540-3571): nu(lambda) = sqrt(4 - lambda^2)/(2 pi) for -2 < lambda < 2, 0 otherwise (printed): the upper edge. Convention (KZ Sec. 3.1-3.2, mapped into rmt/stieltjes.py): A = (G + G^T)/sqrt(2N), G_ij i.i.d. N(0, 1); S(z) = (1/N) sum 1/(lambda_i - z), nu = Im S(x + i0)/pi.
semicircle_edge.independent_route: the cavity recursion S_(N+1) = -1/(z + S_N) (KZ Sec. 3.3) as a Moebius map: parabolic at z^2 = 4 (certified, rmt/stieltjes.py); eigvalsh of sampled Wigner matrices at N = 400 (tests/test_random_matrix.py)

mp_edge_lower_a0p25.cite: F. Krzakala & L. Zdeborova, 'Statistical Physics Methods in Optimization and Machine Learning: An Introduction to Replica, Cavity & Message-Passing techniques', lecture notes, version of June 9 2024 (the PDF read page by page and as text), Exercise 3.1 item 2 (p. 56; notes.txt lines 3699-3703): the Marcenko-Pastur law with lambda_+- = (1 +- sqrt(alpha))^2, printed; the value is its evaluation at alpha = 1/4 (lower edge), mpmath at 40 digits rounded to 30. Convention (KZ Ex. 3.1, mapped into rmt/stieltjes.py): Sigma = X X^T / N, X an M x N matrix of i.i.d. N(0, 1), alpha = M/N (= gamma = p/n of learning/ridge.py, not the regression chapters' alpha = 1/gamma).
mp_edge_lower_a0p25.independent_route: the cavity route of rmt/stieltjes.py: the Wishart Schur-complement recursion S <- 1/(-z + 1/(1 + alpha S)) as a Moebius map turns parabolic (trace^2 = 4 det) exactly at the support edges, certified in arb; and eigvalsh of sampled Wishart matrices (tests/test_random_matrix.py)
